source.title: OTM / SBMD Rearch — Current and Proposed Architecture

scenes.heading: One-Time Mandates
scenes.narration: One-time mandates and single-block-multiple-debit are moving off the Laravel monolith. Here is what changes, in sixty seconds.

scenes.heading: The problem
bullets: Mandate logic split across two gateways
Expiry rules duplicated per merchant category
scenes.narration: Today the mandate rules live in two places, so expiry validation is duplicated and nothing owns the decision to block funds. Every new mandate type means editing both paths.

scenes.heading: Before and after
scenes.narration: The legacy path goes through the monolith and the old gateway. The rearchitected path routes through pg-router into a dedicated mandate service that owns the rules outright.

scenes.heading: The rearch path
scenes.mermaid:
graph TD
  A[Edge] --> B[pg-router]
  B --> C[CPS]
  C --> D[payments-upi]
  D --> E[payments-mandate]
  E --> F[(mandate_setups)]
scenes.narration: A request enters at Edge, and pg-router evaluates a Splitz experiment to decide rearch or legacy. If it is rearch, it flows through CPS and payments-upi into payments-mandate, which persists the mandate setup.

scenes.heading: Watch out for
bullets: Insurance MCCs cap expiry at 14 days
type must be mapped from the token
scenes.narration: Three things bite: a one-time frequency always forces block fund on, and insurance merchant categories cap expiry at fourteen days instead of thirty years. If pg-router does not map the type field off the token, it lands empty in the database.
The full spec has the sequence diagrams and the rollout plan.
